newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to rebuild bomb-damaged Colombo.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to rebuild bomb-damaged Colombo.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Friday unveiled a $400 million plan to rebuild the heart of the capital Colombo, devastated by a Tamil Tiger rebel suicide bomb attack in January.
The plan will complement the expansion of the port, south Asia's trans-shipment hub, Urban Development Authority (UDA) officials told a news conference.
"Historically, this is how the city was built -- around the port," said UDA deputy director-general, Lakshman Jayasekera. "We plan to develop Colombo accordingly."
Under the first phase of the project, the Fort financial district, devastated by the attack, will be completely rebuilt in an entirely new style, he said.
Almost 100 people were killed when a Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam suicide bomber rammed a truck full of explosives into the Central Bank on January 31.
"We have got international sympathy because we are victims of terrorism," Jayasekera said. "The United States, the European Union, Canada and China have offered aid to rebuild Colombo."
The first phase of the work will start in January, with the help of a $110 million soft loan from the United States, and will take about 15 months, he said.
"We do not want to demolish anything unless it is structurally damaged," said Milroy Perera of the Millennium Consortium, which won the deal to rebuild and modernise Colombo.
"We want to retain as much of Colombo Fort as possible," he added. "Fort has always been an island. Our proposal goes back to its origins and Fort becomes an island again."
Under the reconstruction plan, much of the Fort will be pedestrianised, access for vehicles will be restricted and a tramway will be introduced, he said.
The second phase of the project will see the construction of high-rises along the waterfront and the Beira lake, a marina, a green belt and a two-way ring road, he said.
Hotels and office buildings, shopping arcades, luxury apartments and tree-lined areas will also be built, he added.
Jayasekera said the UDA and the private sector, including businesses affected by the bomb attack, have formed an umbrella organisation called Centrepoint Colombo Ltd to supervise the work.
